text:
maria: Heads up — noticed two identical 'Managed GPU support' line items on the Feb invoice, one for us-west1 and one for us-central1, same amount $12,345. Looks like a duplicate charge. Invoice INV-2026-02-17

sam: Can you paste invoice id and attach the line snippet? Also, did we redeploy anything that touched billing account labels?

maria: Invoice ID: 1234567890. Snippet:
```
LineItem: Managed GPU - support
Product: redwood-gpu-support
Region: us-west1
Amount: 12,345.00 USD
Tax: 0.00

LineItem: Managed GPU - support
Region: us-central1
Amount: 12,345.00 USD
```

jeff: Hmm — that's weird. I queried the billing export to BigQuery. Here's the SQL I used (filtered by invoice id):
```
SELECT cost, sku, project, region, usage_start_time
FROM `billing.export.billing_data`
WHERE invoice_id = '1234567890'
AND sku_description LIKE '%Managed GPU%'
ORDER BY usage_start_time;
```
Results show two rows for same sku and same usage_start_time but different zone labels. Could be a zone-aggregation bug at provider level or our tagging duplicated across two billing accounts.

anna: Did we change commitment mapping last week when we moved some capacity to Dedicated? Could credits have been misrouted?

maria: Yes — we shifted 8 A100 GPUs from hosted to dedicated pool on Feb 12. Sam, Jeff — can you check whether commitment credits were applied after that date?

sam: On it. Also opening a support ticket with provider. Draft message:
```
Hi, we see duplicate line items for Managed GPU support on invoice 1234567890. Two identical charges in different regions for the same usage timestamps. Requesting reconciliation and investigation into whether commitment/reservation credits were misapplied.
```

billing-bot: Support case created: CASE-987654. Estimated initial response in 48 hours.

jeff: Quick check — the commit allocation table shows commitment_id CMMT-44 applied to project 'redwood-infra' and to 'redwood-dedicated' in separate namespaces due to a provisioning script that wrote the label twice. Here's the kubectl snippet I found in infra repo that caused it:
```
# accidental double-labeling
kubectl label node gpu-node-12 commitment=CMMT-44
kubectl label node gpu-node-12 commitment=CMMT-44 --overwrite
```

maria: Ugh. Likely wrote the label under both billing accounts when node migrated. Can we revert the duplicate label and ask provider to re-run billing calc?

sam: I've removed the duplicate labels from staging, will roll to prod in 30m. I'll attach the PR.

cloud-support: Quick note from case team: Please also provide CSV of affected line items and proof of label changes (commit hashes). That speeds up reconciliation.

maria: Will upload CSV + commit sha and ping CASE-987654. Also asking finance to withhold payment for the duplicated amount pending provider confirmation. @finance-team :eyes: 

anna: A couple of follow-ups: 1) add a guard in provisioning so labels are idempotent, 2) add an alert when billing export shows identical sku+timestamp duplicates, 3) run a retrospective on the Dedicated migration checklist.

maria: Sounds good. I'll create the checklist items. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
